title: Why the author delayed writing against the new prophecy
english: For a very long and considerable time, beloved Avircius Marcellus, I held back somewhat, even though you had commanded me to write a discourse against the heresy of those called followers of Miltiades. It was not that I lacked the ability to refute the lie and bear witness to the truth. Rather, I was afraid and cautious that I might seem to some people to be writing additions to, or adding new provisions to, the word of the new covenant of the gospel. No one who has chosen to conduct his life according to the gospel may add to that word or take away from it. But recently I was in Ancyra in Galatia, and I found the church there much disturbed by rumor of this new prophecy. It is not, as they themselves say, prophecy, but much more, as will be shown, false prophecy. So, as far as possible, with the Lord granting it, we discussed these very matters and the arguments they put forward on each occasion for several days in the church. As a result, the church rejoiced and was strengthened toward the truth, while those on the opposing side were repulsed for the present and the adversaries were grieved. The local elders then asked that we leave behind some memorandum of what had been said against those who oppose the word of truth, and our fellow elder Zoticus of Otrenus was present as well. This we did not do, but we promised to write and, with the Lord granting it, to send it to them with diligence.
orientation: The author addresses Avircius Marcellus, explaining why he has only now written the treatise against the Cataphrygian heresy that Avircius commissioned.

title: Origin of the new prophecy in Ardabau
english: Their opposition, then, and the recent heresy of their schism against the church had this origin. There is said to be a village in Mysia on the Phrygian border, called Ardabau. There, they say, one of the newly converted, named Montanus, in the time of Gratus, proconsul of Asia, first gave entrance into himself to the adversary through an unbounded desire of soul for preeminence. gave entrance into himself to the adversary through an unbounded desire of soul for preeminence. He was carried by a spirit and, suddenly falling into some kind of possession and ecstasy, began to be possessed, and he started to speak and make strange utterances, supposedly prophesying contrary to the church's custom handed down by tradition and succession from the beginning.

Of those who were present at that time to hear the bastard utterances, some were distressed, treating him as one being worked upon, demonized, and in a spirit of error, and as one troubling the crowds. They rebuked him and tried to stop him from speaking, remembering the Lord's distinction and threat to keep watchful guard against the coming of false prophets (Matthew 7:15). Others, however, were elated as though by a holy spirit and a prophetic spiritual gift, and not least puffed up, forgetting the Lord's distinction. They invited the mind-harming, flattering, people-deceiving spirit, being beguiled and led astray by it, so that it could no longer be stopped from speaking or silenced.

By some artifice, or rather by such a method of evil cunning, the devil devised destruction for those who disobeyed. Since he was being honored by them beyond what he deserved, he stirred up and further inflamed their minds, which had fallen asleep from the faith that is according to truth. He even roused two other women and filled them with the bastard spirit, so that they too spoke frantically, untimely, and in a strange manner, just like the one mentioned before.

The spirit blessed those who rejoiced and boasted in it, puffing them up through the greatness of its promises, though at times it also condemned them outright with plausible, well-aimed accusations, so that it might seem to have the power to convict. But these were only a few of the Phrygians who had been deceived. The self-willed spirit taught them to blaspheme the whole church under heaven, because the false prophetic spirit received neither honor nor entrance into it.

For when the faithful throughout Asia had gathered many times and in many places of Asia for this purpose, and had examined the recent utterances and declared them profane, and had rejected the heresy, then indeed they were expelled from the church and barred from communion.
orientation: The author is beginning the written memorandum requested by the elders, explaining how the Montanist heresy first arose in a village of Phrygian Mysia.
